partitions.title: Strict equality across the ECMAScript Type partition, including ordered evaluation of arbitrarily nested operand expressions
partitions.rationale: The property specification independently crosses the canonical ECMAScript Type partition for both strict-equality operators and observes left-to-right evaluation. The compiler lowers arbitrary source nesting from the expression tree through one sequenced operand worklist, while the runtime helper implements dynamic same-Type comparison. The separately generated native stress case exercises a representative deep right-nested tree and cannot be substituted by property-example cardinality.

clauseEvidence.rationale: One direct terminal partition binds the pinned IsStrictlyEqual scenarios to independent semantic, cardinality, and implementation evidence.

partitions.title: Generic construction, iterator preference and closing, mapping, CreateDataProperty, length finalization, and array-like fallback
partitions.rationale: The independent property crosses iterable and array-like inputs, constructor and non-constructor receivers, constructor arity, ordered mapper validation and invocation, descriptor creation, length finalization, nullish failures, and the distinct mapper/definition/next abrupt-completion closing rules. Array.from consumes one iterator or indexed worklist; the separate generated native case stresses that worklist at representative width. The exact pinned clause query remains authoritative: any unsupported or failing scenario keeps the claim blocked.

clauseEvidence.rationale: The complete Array.from algorithm is represented as one terminal worklist partition with reciprocal property, stress, declaration, runtime, and pinned Test262 evidence.

partitions.title: Generic construction, item-list CreateDataProperty operations, and length finalization
partitions.rationale: The independent property crosses constructor and non-constructor receivers, constructor length delivery, data-property descriptors, failure propagation, stable result ordering, and final length. Array.of consumes the runtime argument list through one canonical worklist; the separate generated native case stresses the same path at representative width. The exact pinned clause query must still pass exhaustively before this evidence can contribute to a claim.

clauseEvidence.rationale: The complete Array.of algorithm is represented as one terminal item-worklist partition with reciprocal property, stress, declaration, runtime, and pinned Test262 evidence.

partitions.title: Case-expression evaluation and Strict Equality selection across ECMAScript Types, identities, suspension, and abrupt completion
partitions.rationale: The independent property derives discriminants and case values from one ECMAScript Type/identity collection, models the evaluated case prefix with Strict Equality, and crosses mixed Types, NaN, signed zero, BigInt, Symbol/Object/Function identity, default placement, fallthrough, abrupt completion, nested awaited discriminators, and awaited cases in both memory modes. One source-ordered clause worklist feeds the ordinary, lazy-generator, and async CFG comparison paths. The separate generated width stress exercises that same worklist without treating clause counts as completion evidence.

clauseEvidence.rationale: The exact CaseClauseIsSelected Test262 scenarios are paired with an independent Type-partition property, representative clause-width stress, retained async E2E regressions, and the one runtime Strict Equality implementation.

partitions.title: Module namespace slot identity, null prototype, non-extensibility, and @@toStringTag dispatch
partitions.rationale: The property specification crosses namespace identity, prototype, integrity, symbol, descriptor, and live-binding behavior. The generated width case independently stresses construction from the canonical export collection.

clauseEvidence.rationale: The observable namespace exotic contract is bound to pinned Test262 metadata plus independent local semantic, cardinality, and implementation evidence.

partitions.title: The namespace prototype is always null
partitions.rationale: The property specification observes the null prototype through direct and Object reflection paths; the separate generated export-width case proves the invariant is independent of namespace cardinality.

clauseEvidence.rationale: The complete observable prototype result is one finite semantic partition over namespaces of arbitrary export width.

partitions.title: Setting null succeeds without change; every different prototype is rejected
partitions.rationale: The property specification crosses Object and Reflect paths for the existing null prototype and a different object prototype. Namespace size is independently stressed.

clauseEvidence.rationale: The same-prototype and changed-prototype outcomes form the exact observable partition.

partitions.title: Every completed namespace is non-extensible
partitions.rationale: The property specification observes the invariant through Object.isExtensible; the generated case proves finalization is independent of export width.

clauseEvidence.rationale: The specified false result is directly evidenced for the canonical namespace representation.

partitions.title: PreventExtensions succeeds on the already non-extensible namespace
partitions.rationale: The property specification exercises integrity operations over a finalized namespace, while the generated case independently stresses finalization over a wide export collection.

clauseEvidence.rationale: The idempotent success result is directly bound to the shared object integrity implementation.

partitions.title: Export descriptors are live writable data descriptors; absent and symbol keys retain their specified behavior and TDZ
partitions.rationale: The property specification crosses initialized and uninitialized live exports, absent keys, symbols, and descriptor attributes. The generated case stresses descriptor-bearing export cardinality.

clauseEvidence.rationale: Property-key and binding-state semantics are one partition over the canonical export collection.

partitions.title: Compatible export redefinitions succeed without mutation; incompatible or absent definitions fail
partitions.rationale: The property specification crosses empty, same-value, changed-value, and throwing Object/Boolean Reflect outcomes. The generated namespace width is a distinct cardinality proof.

clauseEvidence.rationale: Descriptor compatibility, rather than fixture shape, defines this terminal partition.

partitions.title: Presence follows the namespace export set without reading an absent or symbol binding
partitions.rationale: The property specification crosses exported, absent, unknown-symbol, and well-known-symbol keys. The generated case independently stresses the canonical export-key collection.

clauseEvidence.rationale: Presence is derived from the one canonical PropertyKey collection.

partitions.title: Export reads resolve the current binding value; absent and unsupported symbol reads yield undefined
partitions.rationale: The property specification mutates live bindings and crosses data, function, class, absent, and symbol reads. The generated case stresses reads from a wide canonical export collection.

clauseEvidence.rationale: Live binding lookup and non-export keys are crossed in one property-key partition.

partitions.title: Every namespace write returns false regardless of key or receiver
partitions.rationale: The property specification crosses exported, absent, and symbol writes through strict assignment and Reflect. The generated width case proves rejection is independent of export cardinality.

clauseEvidence.rationale: All receiver and PropertyKey forms converge on the namespace [[Set]] rejection path.

partitions.title: Deleting an export fails and deleting an absent property key succeeds
partitions.rationale: The property specification crosses exported, absent, and symbol deletion through strict syntax and Reflect. The generated case independently stresses the canonical export collection.

clauseEvidence.rationale: Export membership determines the exact delete outcome for every PropertyKey.

partitions.title: OwnPropertyKeys returns sorted export strings followed by @@toStringTag
partitions.rationale: The property specification checks public PropertyKey types and ordering. The generated width case is the independent representative stress for arbitrary export-list width.

clauseEvidence.rationale: One canonical raw PropertyKey list feeds the Object and Reflect projections.

partitions.title: One sorted resolved export plan creates one finalized namespace object per Module Record
partitions.rationale: The emitter consumes one resolved export collection, emits live getters, and lazily memoizes one namespace factory. Property and generated evidence cover semantic partitions and representative export width.

clauseEvidence.rationale: The creation algorithm is represented by one canonical export plan and one cardinality-independent factory emitter.

partitions.title: ResolveExport follows explicit and star edges, excludes default from stars, detects ambiguity, and terminates cycles
partitions.rationale: The property specification crosses explicit, indirect, namespace, deep star, default-exclusion, ambiguity, and cycle-safe self-import semantics. The generated width case is independent stress.

clauseEvidence.rationale: Resolution is proved from the Module Record graph and declaration identity, not from enumerated re-export fixture families.

partitions.title: Source Text Module ResolveExport traverses the canonical Module Record graph by binding identity
partitions.rationale: The property specification exercises Source Text Module local, indirect, star, ambiguous, and namespace resolutions using checker declaration identity; a distinct generated case stresses export width.

clauseEvidence.rationale: The source-text specialization shares the one cycle-guarded ResolveExport graph traversal.

partitions.title: GetModuleNamespace returns the lazily created singleton for the resolved Module Record
partitions.rationale: The property specification checks repeated imports and deep namespace re-exports for identity. The generated case independently stresses singleton creation over a wide export collection.

clauseEvidence.rationale: A WeakMap keyed by the canonical Source Text Module record selects one lazily emitted namespace plan.

partitions.title: Reflection exposes the Module Namespace Exotic Object contract without substituting an ordinary object
partitions.rationale: The property specification exercises Object and Reflect observation of namespace internal methods and keys; the generated width case independently stresses the underlying export collection.

clauseEvidence.rationale: The Reflection contract is tied to the same non-ordinary runtime representation and exact observable tests.

groups.title: Scope
groups.rationale: Normative framing; the validator must still confirm that every observable descendant elsewhere is classified.

groups.title: Conformance
knownGaps: Normative-optional choices and forbidden extensions have not been audited.
groups.rationale: The claim report must disclose optional choices; example subclauses are not implementation requirements.

groups.title: Normative References
knownGaps: Unicode and numeric dependency versions are not yet attested in run artifacts.
groups.rationale: Dependency identity is attestation evidence rather than a Test262 result.

groups.title: Overview
groups.rationale: Descriptive definitions are discharged by the corresponding normative clauses.

groups.title: Notational Conventions
groups.rationale: Specification notation is not directly executable; referenced algorithms remain required.

groups.title: ECMAScript Data Types and Values
knownGaps: Exact clause evidence and semantic partitions remain unverified against the pinned suite.

groups.title: Abstract Operations
knownGaps: Abstract-operation coverage must be derived transitively from exact esid mappings and reviewed gap evidence.

groups.title: Syntax-Directed Operations
knownGaps: There is no complete clause-level mapping for shared syntax-directed operations.

groups.title: Executable Code and Execution Contexts
knownGaps: Fresh Realm and separate Script evaluation are missing from the Test262 host profile.

groups.title: Ordinary and Exotic Objects Behaviours
knownGaps: Pinned namespace scenarios that depend on general super lowering remain unsupported; exact ordinary/Proxy/Symbol PropertyKey clause partitions and namespace-proxy interactions are not yet clause-verified.

groups.title: ECMAScript Language: Source Text
knownGaps: Compiler parsing currently depends on the pinned TypeScript parser and is not yet attested for ES2026 source text.

groups.title: ECMAScript Language: Lexical Grammar
knownGaps: Positive and negative lexical grammar have not been run with exact Test262 parse-phase classification.

groups.title: ECMAScript Language: Expressions
knownGaps: General call-spread, yielded expressions, and remaining suspension graphs are incomplete.

groups.title: ECMAScript Language: Statements and Declarations
knownGaps: Generator/async abrupt-completion and iterator-close graphs remain incomplete.

groups.title: ECMAScript Language: Functions and Classes
knownGaps: General generator state machines, async generators, and remaining async suspension graphs are incomplete.

groups.title: ECMAScript Language: Scripts and Modules
knownGaps: Synchronous cyclic Module graphs now separate graph-wide declaration instantiation from source-ordered evaluation; asynchronous cyclic evaluation, non-finite dynamic host loading and remaining ImportCall suspension/object-model partitions, top-level await, and namespace scenarios blocked by general super lowering remain incomplete.

groups.title: Error Handling and Language Extensions
knownGaps: Exact thrown constructor identity is not exposed by the conformance host.

groups.title: ECMAScript Standard Built-in Objects
knownGaps: Broad built-in path evidence must be refined to exact clauses before verification; Function source text, @@hasInstance, dynamic source construction, and ordinary variadic activations remain open.

groups.title: The Global Object
knownGaps: Runtime eval needs a non-delegating, general Script implementation for full conformance; Reflect operations still require exact clause partitions and exhaustive pinned Test262 evidence.

groups.title: Fundamental Objects
knownGaps: Clause-level descriptor, prototype, Symbol, and realm behavior remains unverified; Function source text, @@hasInstance, dynamic source construction, and ordinary variadic activations remain open.

groups.title: Numbers and Dates
knownGaps: IEEE-754 edge behavior and the full Date algorithm surface remain unverified.

groups.title: Text Processing
knownGaps: PCRE2 behavior is not yet demonstrated equivalent to every ECMA-262 RegExp algorithm.

groups.title: Indexed Collections
knownGaps: TypedArray and full array exotic semantics remain unverified.

groups.title: Keyed Collections
knownGaps: All iterator-close, mutation-during-iteration, and weak-key partitions require pinned verification.

groups.title: Structured Data
knownGaps: Shared memory, Atomics, detachment, and complete JSON semantics are not verified.

groups.title: Managing Memory
knownGaps: The Test262 host lacks the required gc hook and finalization job protocol.

groups.title: Control Abstraction Objects
knownGaps: General generators, async generators, remaining async CFGs, and full iterator close semantics are incomplete.

groups.title: Reflection
knownGaps: Exact terminal clause registration and the remaining Reflect/Proxy internal-method semantic partitions are unverified.

groups.title: Memory Model
knownGaps: The Test262 host lacks agents and the project has no complete ECMAScript shared-memory implementation.

groups.title: Normative Annex B — Additional ECMAScript Features for Web Browsers
knownGaps: An unqualified claim includes Annex B here; IsHTMLDDA and the remaining legacy surface are not implemented.
